key_insight: Transient gust forcing drives wall turbulence into a non-equilibrium state, shifting energy toward low-frequency coherent structures and sharply increasing extreme near-wall events.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and mitigate unsteady aerodynamic loads on UAVs and other wall-bounded flow systems operating in gusty atmospheric conditions.
method: Direct numerical simulations (DNS) under Gaussian-type cyclostationary gust forcing
Spectral and continuous wavelet analysis of turbulent structure evolution
Two-step conditional averaging for rare backflow and extreme wall-shear events
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a frequency lock between coherent structures and gust forcing with only 2.4% deviation, and up to an order-of-magnitude rise in extreme event probability under severe forcing.
watch_item: The findings are based on DNS and a specific Gaussian-type transient forcing model, so transferability to real atmospheric gust spectra and higher-Re industrial flows should be validated.
paper_title: Triggering of extreme events and coherent-structure modulation in wall-turbulence under cyclostationary forces
